semantics.clock: All sequential logic triggers on positive clk edges, as specified.
semantics.sample_relation: Immediately after positive edge n, anyedge equals the bitwise difference between input sampled at edge n and input sampled at edge n-1, held until the next positive edge.
semantics.transition: Both 0-to-1 and 1-to-0 sampled transitions produce a one for that bit; equal successive samples produce zero.
semantics.initialization: No reset or initial values are specified. Previous sample and registered output are uninitialized; first-edge comparison with an unknown previous sample is unknown. Fully known samples establish defined behavior from the second edge.

numeric.operation: Independent bit comparisons; no signed arithmetic, overflow, or cross-bit dependence.
numeric.four_state: Unknown sample bits propagate through the bitwise change comparison.

verification.oracle: Compare each bit of successive sampled inputs using equality/inequality, grounded in the original change-detection requirement.
verification.sampling: Drive away from rising edges and check after nonblocking assignments settle; verify output holds between rising edges.
cases: Changes between edges returning to the previous value
verification.termination: Fatal on mismatch, bounded timeout, PASS only after every check succeeds.

specification_ambiguities.evidence: The original supplies no reset or initialization requirement.
specification_ambiguities.resolution: Do not introduce initialization or reset; defined functional checks begin after history is established. Unknown startup is checked as the natural uninitialized sequential behavior.

specification_ambiguities.evidence: Changes are described from one clock cycle to the next, with output set the cycle after a transition and all sequential logic positive-edge triggered.
specification_ambiguities.resolution: Register the comparison of current sampled input with the preceding sample at each positive edge; no additional pipeline stage.
